page.text:
In the `satisfies:` section, you'll notice two ways "in" is used.
First, it is used as `forAll: X "in" A` and later as `X "in"? B`
(note the `?`).

The first `X "in" A` is a *specification* and introduces a symbol `X`
that is an element of `A`. Every specification automatically as an
associated statement form specified by using the `?` suffix. In this case
the statement `X "in"? B` represents the question of whether or not `X`
is an element of `B`.

Similar to `"op"` specifications, infix describes also have an
associated statement form automatically available for them. For example,
for the `A \:subset:/ B` infix describes we defined that introduces, `A`
as a set that is a subset of `B`, one can write `A \:subset?:/ C` which
represents the statement that asks if `A` is a subset of `C`.

Thus specifications introduce symbols, and statements communicate
questions that may be true or false about symbols that already exist.
